simple.meaning: פִּגּוּל (piggûwl) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, fetid , i.e. (figuratively) unclean (ceremonially).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּגּוּל (H6292) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 7:18, with occurrences in Leviticus, Isaiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּגּוּל (H6292) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּגּוּל (H6292) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּגּוּל (piggûwl) / H6292 is traced through Leviticus 7:18, Leviticus 19:7, Isaiah 65:4, Ezekiel 4:14 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6292. piggul [ מִּגּוּל ] noun masculine Lev 7:18 foul thing, refuse , but only as technical term of unclean sacrificial flesh; — it is ׳פ if eaten on third day 7:18 (P), 19:7 (H); compare פ ׳בְּשַׂר Ezek 4:14 (undefined); plural מִּגֻּלִים מְרַק Isa 65:4 broth of refuse things (Kt פרק ), RS Sem i. 325, 2nd ed. 343 thinks of flesh with the blood; Du on the passage of mice and other unclean animals .
definitions.rootNote: or פִּגֻּל ; from an unused root meaning to stink ;
